Definition: sterile (as wrapped up too hard); figuratively, desolate
BiblicalUsage: Galmud means sterile, wrapped up too hard to bear fruit, and then desolate. Zion asks who has begotten her children, seeing she has lost them and is desolate in Isaiah 49:21, and the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate in Job 15:34. Job's friends were solitary, fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste, in Job 30:3, and Job curses the night to be solitary in Job 3:7.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe desolation is the fruit of hypocrisy and the cry of the afflicted alike. The hypocrite's house is desolate and Job's night is solitary, yet God answers both. I hold that the desolate are not forgotten, for God promises to comfort Zion.
